report.tagline: A global app to book rides, order food and groceries, and ship freight, connecting riders and eaters with independent drivers and couriers.
report.simpleSummary: You open Uber, type where you want to go, see the price, and a nearby driver picks you up in a few minutes. The same app lets you order food and groceries through Uber Eats. Uber does not own the cars; drivers use their own and Uber takes a cut of each fare. A monthly membership, Uber One, gives discounts on both rides and delivery, and Uber is now adding driverless cars from partners like Waymo.

overview.whatItDoes: Uber runs a marketplace that matches people who need a ride or delivery with drivers and couriers who want to earn. It started in San Francisco in 2009 and now operates in about 70 countries. It makes money by keeping a share of each fare or order, plus fees from restaurants, ads and Uber One memberships. Its CEO is Dara Khosrowshahi.
howItWorks: A rider enters a destination and sees an upfront price, set by distance, time and demand.
When demand is higher than nearby drivers, surge pricing raises the fare to attract more drivers and calm demand.
Uber matches the rider with the nearest available driver; the driver accepts and drives in their own car.
Payment is charged in the app; Uber keeps a share and pays the driver weekly or instantly.
Uber Eats works the same way with restaurants and stores, and couriers deliver.
In some cities, robotaxis from partners like Waymo and WeRide take rides booked in the Uber app.
overview.valueProposition: A ride or delivery anywhere in minutes with a known price, and flexible earnings for millions of drivers.

businessModel.summary: Uber earns a share of every ride and delivery. Riders pay the fare; Uber keeps roughly a quarter to a third after paying drivers (varies by market). Delivery adds restaurant commissions and fees. Ads, Uber One and freight add more.

revenueStreams.detail: Share of ride fares and booking fees; $7.5 billion revenue in Q3 2026.
Restaurant commissions, customer fees and ads; $5.5 billion in Q3 2026.
Matching truckers with shippers; $1.8 billion in Q3 2026.
Sponsored listings on Uber Eats and in-ride ads.
$9.99 a month or $96 a year in the US.

businessModel.pricing: Upfront prices that change with distance, time and demand. Uber One costs $9.99 a month in the US. Restaurants pay commission tiers of roughly 15% to 30%. Prices vary by country.
costDrivers: Legal and regulatory costs, including driver classification
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $25 US ride, Uber might keep about $6 to $7 after paying the driver (estimate), from which it pays insurance, payment processing, support and marketing. Company-wide, Uber keeps about 3.9% of gross bookings as operating profit, so roughly $1 profit on that ride. On a $40 Eats order, its cut is lower, but ads and Uber One improve the margin. Profit grows as each driver gets more trips per hour.

howTheyGetUsers: Brand recognition: 'Uber' is a verb in many countries
Referral credits for riders and bonuses for new drivers
Launching in new cities and adding new products like Moto and Auto in India
whatBringsUsersBack: Habit for commutes and nights out
Uber One savings across rides and food
growth.moat: Uber has a network effect in each city: more riders keep drivers busy, which lowers wait times, which brings more riders. Being in about 70 countries with both rides and delivery lets drivers switch between the two, keeping them busy. Robotaxi companies partner with Uber because it already has the riders.

improvementIdeas.idea: Price lock: let riders lock a fare for 10 minutes during surge
improvementIdeas.problem: Riders feel surge is unfair and unpredictable.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer abandoned requests and more trust.

improvementIdeas.idea: Penalise and reduce driver cancellations with better trip info upfront
One-tap Uber One cancellation with clear savings summary
improvementIdeas.problem: Hard cancellation hurts trust and invites regulation.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better brand trust and lower regulatory risk.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Uber One net promoter score and churn

improvementIdeas.idea: Mixed fleets: auto-route short city trips to robotaxis when cheaper
improvementIdeas.problem: High driver cost in some cities.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower cost per trip and better margins.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Robotaxi trips share and cost per trip

pmLessons: Marketplaces must balance two sides. Surge pricing is a tool to match supply and demand, but it costs trust.
Bundling products with one membership like Uber One raises how much each user spends.
Partnering can beat building. Uber dropped its own self-driving unit and now partners with robotaxi firms.
Watch the right metric. Revenue fell in rides while bookings grew, because of how money was counted in some countries.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you decide the price of a ride during a concert ending?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain supply vs demand, rider willingness to pay, driver incentives and fairness. Propose surge caps or price lock and metrics like conversion and wait time.

interviewQuestions.question: Uber One sign-ups are growing but ride frequency is flat. Why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment members by use. Perhaps members only use Eats. Propose ride perks and measure cross-use.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Uber build its own robotaxis or partner?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost, speed, risk and control. Uber's strength is demand. Discuss the risk of partners going direct.

interviewQuestions.question: Driver cancellations went up in one city. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split by trip distance, area, time, pay. Check if drivers see trips as unprofitable. Fix incentives or info shown.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Uber's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Total trips completed. Break into users, frequency, reliability and supply.
